'''Joseph Arkin''' ({{birth date|1923|5|25}} – {{Death date|2002|8|5}}) was a mathematician, lecturer and professor at the [[United States Military Academy|West Point military academy]].<ref name=arney>{{cite web |url=http://www.dean.usma.edu/math/people/rickey/dms/Non-grads/Arkin-retire.htm |author=David C. Arney |title=Biography of Joseph Arkin An American Ramanujan |year=1994 |accessdate=October 17, 2012 }}</ref><ref name=ams>{{cite journal |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200210/inside.pdf |year=2002 |title=Inside the AMS |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |volume=49 |issue=10 |page=1276 }}</ref>

Originally from Brooklyn, New York, Professor Joseph "Joe" Arkin was married for 48 years to Judith Lobel Arkin. They had four daughters, Helen, Aviva, Jessica and Sarah.

Professor Joseph Arkin worked at the Department of Mathematical Sciences at the [[United States Military Academy]] since 1986, until he retired from the faculty on September 23, 1994.<ref name=arney/> He also spent time as a visiting lecturer at Princeton and The New York Academy of Sciences. He was a member of the [[American Mathematical Society]] since 1964,<ref name=ams/> and member of the [[The Fibonacci Association|Fibonacci Association]] since 1965.<ref name=arney/>

Most of his contributions and collaborative academic research was in the branch of [[number theory]].<ref name=arney/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dean.usma.edu/math/people/rickey/dms/Non-grads/Arkin-pubs.htm |title=Publications of Joseph Arkin |publisher=U.S. Military Academy |year=2002 |access-date=2012-10-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090114112903/http://www.dean.usma.edu/math/people/rickey/dms/Non-grads/Arkin-pubs.htm |archive-date=2009-01-14 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He authored and co-authored publications, in collaboration with notable mathematicians like [[Paul Erdős]], [[Ronald Graham]], [[Ernst G. Straus|E.G. Straus]], [[Richard M. Pollack|Richard Pollack]], [[Vern Hoggatt]], [[Paul A. Smith|Paul Smith]], V.E. Smith, [[Gerald Bergum]], and [[Stefan Burr]], among others.<ref name="Arkin 1989 296–302">{{cite journal |journal=Fibonacci Quarterly |title=Unique Fibonacci Formulas |last1=Arkin |first1=Joseph |last2=Arney |first2=D.C. |last3=Bergum |first3=G .E. |last4=Burr |first4=Stephan A. |last5=Porter |first5=B. J. |volume=27 |issue=4 |year=1989 |pages=296–302 |url=http://www.fq.math.ca/Scanned/27-4/arkin1.pdf }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |journal=The Fibonacci Quarterly |last1=Arkin |first1=Joseph |last2= Hoggatt |first2=V. E. |last3=Straus |first3=E. G. |title=On Euler's Solution to a Problem of Diophantus |year=1979 |volume=17 |pages=333–339 |url=http://www.fq.math.ca/Scanned/18-2/arkin.pdf }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |journal=Fibonacci Quarterly |title=Trebly-magic systems in a Latin 3-cube of order eight |last1=Arkin |first1=Joseph |last2=Smith |first2=Paul |volume=14 |issue=2 |year=1976 |pages=167–70 |url=http://www.fq.math.ca/Scanned/14-2/arkin.pdf }}</ref>

Many of his studies have appeared in publications such as the ''[[Mathematics Magazine]]'', ''[[Fibonacci Quarterly]]'', ''[http://www.siam.org/journals/sirev.php SIAM Review]'', ''[[Duke Mathematical Journal]]'', ''[[Journal of Recreational Mathematics]]'', and in Notices of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref name=arney/>

Arkin also published papers in the ''[[Canadian Journal of Mathematics]]'', the ''[[Pacific Journal of Mathematics]]'', and the ''[[Mathematics and Computer Education Journal]]''.<ref name=arney/>
